page: UpCloud PREMIUM-48xCPU-96GB is an x86_64 architecture server powered by an AMD EPYC 9575F processor running at 2.0 GHz. It features 48 physical cores and 48 vCPUs under a shared CPU allocation model, utilizing the KVM hypervisor. The system is equipped with 96.0 GB of system memory, providing a resource density of 2.0 GB per core. Local storage consists of a bundled 400 GB SSD, and the configuration includes one complimentary public IPv4 address. No dedicated GPU hardware is present.

Benchmark data indicates top-tier CPU performance, with stress-ng single-core and multi-core metrics placing in the top 10% of tested systems. Single-threaded gzip compression and bzip3 decompression also rank in the top 10%, alongside multi-threaded bzip3 decompression. Memory bandwidth is strong, with read-only cached small block speeds reaching 6024.49 GB/sec and uncached large block read speeds at 261.26 GB/sec. However, PassMark memory scores fall into the average tier, representing a potential bottleneck relative to the high-compute capabilities.

With a 1:2 vCPU-to-RAM ratio, this server is configured for compute-heavy workloads rather than memory-intensive applications. It demonstrates strong performance in database operations and static web serving, both ranking in the top 25%. LLM inference benchmarks show top-tier prompt processing speeds for small models, though text generation speeds for medium models remain average. This profile is suitable for multi-threaded batch processing, compression tasks, and web serving workloads where raw CPU execution is prioritized over massive memory capacity.
